title: Gateway uplink holdoff buffer for transient internet outages
description: Problem: When the gateway's Yggdrasil/IP uplink is momentarily unavailable, mesh-originated packets for internet destinations are dropped immediately. Brief blips (seconds) cause permanent packet loss. Fix: Add a gateway-only holdoff buffer (same pattern as TX queue — bounded, with deadlines, priority-ordered). Size 8-16 packets. Packets queued when uplink is down; drained when uplink recovers. Deadline expiry prevents bufferbloat if uplink stays down. This buffer exists ONLY in the gateway, NEVER in mesh nodes — mesh nodes always forward toward the gateway and get backpressure via the existing forward buffer. Spec impact: document in spec/08-gateway-coordination.md.
design: New struct UplinkHoldoff in lichen-gateway. Same TxQueue pattern: heapless::BinaryHeap<UplinkItem, Max, 16>. UplinkItem has deadline (30s default), priority (from mesh packet), payload. On uplink recovery: drain oldest-first. On deadline expiry: drop + log. Backpressure: when holdoff full, drop lowest-priority packet (same preemption as TX queue). Python gateway: same pattern with list + heapq. C: not applicable (gateways are Rust/Python, not Zephyr firmware).
